Kube-proxy flags are silently ignored when `--config` is set. This PR makes flags take precedence on the proxy component configuration.

> @thockin this is the thing you were looking for, `mergo`, good job discovering it @hanlins !

Credits to @aojea!

This takes kube-proxy in a different direction than other components (kube-scheduler explicitly makes config and flags exclusive, with the exception of a few deprecated flags).

Whether or not flags should override config generally has been long-debated (cc @mtaufen @deads2k @sttts). I am of the opinion they should not, since it makes inspection/validation of a config file in isolation difficult to understand without also having the full invocation it is a part of.

Hi @liggitt, there're lots of back and forth on this flag precedence behavior, and I agree with your points. But one key difference between components like `kube-scheduler` and `kube-proxy` is `kube-proxy` sometimes needs instance-specific configurations, so in this sense, it's more similar to `kubelet` rather than `kube-scheduler`. Originally we plan to just use `--config` and `--instance-config` to cover both cases, but as you know https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/pull/1439 has been out for a while, but it still has some gaps to fill and could take a few more releases to get there. 
Before that instance-specific config happens, the only thing user have for per-instance config is the flags, but most of the flags are just silently ignored, it's like we want to provide people a better semantics for configurations in the future, we gave them one which is not ideal and the one we gave is not working. Last time during the WG meeting @thockin mentioned that we want to make our existing flag users happy, and we want to do flag overwriting similar to `kubelet` if the cost is not too large. So we take this direction on fixing the flag overwriting for our existing users.

> we want to do flag overwriting similar to `kubelet`

Having reviewed the kubelet flag/config merging changes originally, and many fixup changes over the years, I would strongly recommend against that path. The kubelet config initialization path is almost incomprehensible.

hmm... so, @liggitt are you suggesting, for now that we:
- eliminate these flags entirely  ?   
- fail if config + flags overlap ? 
- just keep doing what we currently do (silently ignore flags) ? 

i guess the current situation as @hanlins sais is the worst case scenario for sure - we have flags, and we ignore them entirely
"fail if config + flags overlap" avoids adding complex new merge behavior, and avoids the footgun of ignored flags. I'd start with that.

Hi @liggitt @knabben, made some updates here. I have to add some struct tag to associate the fields in `KubeProxyConfiguration` with the flags people use. With the change, we can detect and fast fail if the user sets the field in kube-proxy config and also sets the flag for it. But, to address the issue where people's flags got ignored silently, we still need to aggregate the configs from the config file and flags to one place, but since we've already checked that there's no conflict between config file and flags, we can safely combine the two without worry about the precedence. Any opinion on that?

> With the change, we can detect and fast fail if the user sets the field in kube-proxy config and also sets the flag for it.

What's the benefit to letting them set via config file field and flag but only when they match?

How does this determine the difference between a default value in the config and an explicitly set value in the config?

> What's the benefit to letting them set via config file field and flag but only when they match?
> 
> How does this determine the difference between a default value in the config and an explicitly set value in the config?

Actually, if the config is set in both the config file and the flag, no matter if they have the same value or not, we will consider this as a conflict and fail the command. In the test I have I'm using different values but actually it doesn't matter.

In our detection logic, we're actually detecting if the flag value is explicitly set by the user, or it's something from the flag default https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/9a9960d886dac65fc0cba17b99d50c3e546a5779/cmd/kube-proxy/app/server.go#L478
Basically, it's using this [Changed](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/spf13/pflag#FlagSet.Changed) interface to detect whether the flag is set by user or not.

Added a test to demonstrate that if config and flag are both set with the same value, we'll still detect the conflict and error out https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/bdf14d12858fc95212e006536e5480e1bd022d4d/cmd/kube-proxy/app/server_test.go#L692-L698

> Whether or not flags should override config generally has been long-debated (cc @mtaufen @deads2k @sttts). I am of the opinion they should not, since it makes inspection/validation of a config file in isolation difficult to understand without also having the full invocation it is a part of.

I'm in agreement with this. We did it in kubelet because we were pursuing an incremental migration across releases and were trying to keep things backwards compatible when a flag later became available in config, but might still be set on the command line in an existing configuration. But if you can keep it either-or, the implementation is much simpler.

issue_context.title: kube-proxy flags are not respected when using config file together
issue_context.body:
1. With following config file and start kube-proxy with flags `--config=/tmp/kube-proxy.yaml --master=https://localhost:6443 --profiling=true`. 
```
cat <<EOF > /tmp/kube-proxy.yaml
apiVersion: kubeproxy.config.k8s.io/v1alpha1
kind: KubeProxyConfiguration
clientConnection:
  kubeconfig: /var/run/kubernetes/kube-proxy.kubeconfig
hostnameOverride: 127.0.0.1
mode:
featureGates:
  AllAlpha: false
EOF
```

2. Try to access the debug endpoint, you'll get 404
```
curl 127.0.0.1:10249/debug/pprof/
404 page not found

```


Actually, not only the `profiling` flag does not take effect, all other flags which are not set in config file, are all changed to default value and then do not take effect.

review_comments: This type is shared between multiple components (including out-of-tree components), so these flags are determined by the consuming component.

I see. I checked other components like kubelet, and they used the same flag for the same field, but I wasn't aware that maybe some external components are also consuming them. Would it be better if I mark make the struct tag something more specific to kube-proxy? Like change the tag from `flag` to `kubeProxyFlag`?
